claims.text: The baseline is a near-equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA in an as-cast or arc-melted state.
The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy has high density because of heavy elements such as Hf and Ta.
The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr microstructure is prone to forming a continuous ordered B2 phase.
Replacing heavy refractory elements with lighter V will reduce alloy density.
Adjusting the Ti:Zr ratio will favor a disordered BCC matrix over an ordered B2 matrix.
A suitable heat treatment can refine the grain size of the modified alloy.
V addition can stabilize a disordered BCC solid solution without excessive ordering.
A continuous ordered B2 matrix causes poor room-temperature ductility in B2+BCC RHEAs.
Suppressing the continuous ordered B2 phase and promoting disordered BCC will improve room-temperature ductility in the proposed Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr-V alloy.
Solid-solution strengthening and grain-boundary strengthening in a fine-grained BCC matrix can maintain high strength.
The modified alloy will have more than 10% lower density than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will have room-temperature yield strength above 1000 MPa.
The modified alloy will have total room-temperature elongation above 5%.
Near-equiatomic NbMoTaW has room-temperature yield strength above 1000 MPa and low room-temperature ductility.
Conventional Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEAs typically have yield strength above 1000 MPa and ductility below 2% because of a continuous ordered B2 phase.
Excess V beyond its solubility limit would induce brittle intermetallic compounds such as Laves phases.
An unsuitable Ti:Zr ratio can trigger renewed formation of ordered B2.
Brittle oxides or intermetallic phases formed during processing could negate ductility gains.
Vacuum arc melting or spark plasma sintering will ensure adequate compositional homogeneity.

contradictions.description: The proposed baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr composition contains no W, yet the main intervention is described as substituting a portion of its W. Qualifiers such as 'if present' do not define a consistent starting alloy.

The predicted density reduction is greater than 10%, whereas the falsification rule only requires greater than 5%. A result between 5% and 10% would contradict the prediction without necessarily falsifying the hypothesis under the stated rule.
